## US-4127 — Update order status from the order detail page

### What changed
Added a `PATCH /orders/{id}/status` endpoint that lets Support agents update an order's status to `Shipped` (or any valid status in the `Pending|Shipped|Delivered|Cancelled` set) directly from the order detail page.

### Why
Support currently emails logistics for ~400 status updates per week, with each hand-off taking 20–40 minutes and occasionally getting lost. Letting agents update the status directly removes most of that manual work and reduces the delay between dispatch and the customer seeing "Shipped" from hours to minutes.

### What's included
- **Controller**: `OrdersController.UpdateStatus` gated to the `Support` role.
- **DTO**: `UpdateOrderStatusRequest` with validation restricting `Status` to the allowed values.
- **Service**: `OrderService.UpdateStatusAsync` updates the order status and sets `StatusUpdatedAt` to `DateTime.UtcNow`.
- **Database**: Migration script `20261101_add_status_updated_at.sql` adds the new `StatusUpdatedAt` column.
- **Tests**: Added `UpdateStatus_ReturnsNoContent_WhenOrderExists` covering the happy path.

### Acceptance criteria
- [x] An agent with the **Support** role can change an order's status to `Shipped` from the order detail page.
- [x] The change records the timestamp of the status update via `StatusUpdatedAt`.
- [x] The endpoint rejects requests from users without the **Support** role via `[Authorize(Roles = "Support")]`.

### Notes
- Returns `204 No Content` on success and `404 Not Found` when the order does not exist.
- Status input is validated with `RegularExpression` to prevent invalid status values.
</Output>
<Rubric>
The "Why?" field explains the business reason stated in the User Story (support handling ~400 manual status updates per week, 20-40 minute hand-offs, hours-to-minutes delay), not a restatement of the code change.

# BUG-3388 — Fix checkout 500 error when cart has no discount

## Summary

Fixes a null-reference exception in `OrderService.GetTotal` that caused checkout to fail when an order had no discount record. The change now safely treats a missing discount as 0% and keeps the order total unchanged.

## Root Cause

`GetTotal` was accessing `order.Discount.Percentage` without checking whether `Discount` was null. For carts with no discount applied, `order.Discount` is `null`, which threw an exception and returned HTTP 500 to the shopper. This impacted ~180 orders (2.1% of checkouts) last week.

## Changes

- **src/Application/Orders/OrderService.cs**
  - Use null-conditional access (`?.`) with a default of `0m` when reading `order.Discount.Percentage`.
  - Renamed local variable from `discount` to `discountPercentage` for clarity.

- **tests/Orders/OrderServiceTests.cs**
  - Added `GetTotal_ReturnsSubtotal_WhenDiscountIsNull` to verify orders with a null discount return the full subtotal.

## Verification

- [x] New unit test passes: `GetTotal_ReturnsSubtotal_WhenDiscountIsNull` (expected total = `100m` for a `50m × 2` line with no discount).
- [x] Existing discount test still passes: `GetTotal` with a 10% discount returns `90m`.
- [x] Acceptance criteria met:
  - Placing an order with no discount completes without an exception.
  - The order total is unchanged when no discount is applied.

---

**Reviewers:** Please confirm there are no other code paths that dereference `order.Discount` without a null check.
</Output>
<Rubric>
The "Why?" field explains the business reason from the User Story (2.1% of checkouts failing, about 180 orders, customers abandoning the cart), not a restatement of the code.

</Rubric>"}]

**TECH-91: Extract pricing rules out of OrderService**

## What

Moves all order pricing logic from `OrderService` into a new, dedicated `PriceCalculator` class and makes `OrderService.GetTotal` delegate to it.

## Why

`OrderService` had grown to 1,400 lines, and every pricing change required touching order orchestration code. By extracting the calculation rules, the pricing team can iterate independently and pricing-related reviews become smaller and faster.

## Changes

- Added `src/Application/Orders/PriceCalculator.cs` with:
  - `Subtotal(Order)` — sum of `UnitPrice * Quantity` across all lines
  - `DiscountAmount(Order)` — discount percentage applied to subtotal
  - `Total(Order)` — `Subtotal - DiscountAmount`
- Updated `OrderService` to hold a `PriceCalculator` instance and call `_pricing.Total(order)` from `GetTotal`.
- Added `GetTotal_MatchesPriceCalculator_ForDiscountedOrder` test to guard that `OrderService.GetTotal` stays in sync with the new calculator.

## Verification

- No behaviour changes; all existing tests continue to pass.
- New test asserts `OrderService.GetTotal` returns the same value as `PriceCalculator.Total` for a discounted order.
</Output>
<Rubric>
The "Why?" field explains the business reason from the User Story (OrderService is 1,400 lines, every pricing change touches it, the pricing team wants to change rules without touching order orchestration), not a restatement of the code.

prompt.raw:
Write a PR description for these code changes.

User Story:
# US-4190 — Rename customerName to customerFullName in the order API

## User story

As an API consumer, I want the order payload to use customerFullName, so that the field name matches what it actually contains.

## Business context

The field returns the first and last name concatenated, but its name suggests only the first name. Two partner integrations already misread it and displayed the wrong value to their users. Renaming now avoids more bad data downstream.

## Acceptance criteria

- The order API returns customerFullName instead of customerName.
- The database column is renamed to match.
- Existing integrations are told the field was renamed.

Code changes:
diff --git a/src/Api/Dtos/OrderDto.cs b/src/Api/Dtos/OrderDto.cs
index 3c7a1b9..8d2e4f5 100644
--- a/src/Api/Dtos/OrderDto.cs
+++ b/src/Api/Dtos/OrderDto.cs
@@ -8,7 +8,7 @@ public sealed record OrderDto(
     int Id,
     string Reference,
     decimal Total,
-    string CustomerName,
+    string CustomerFullName,
     string Status);

index 2b9c4d1..5e7f3a8 100644
--- a/src/Application/Orders/OrderMapper.cs
+++ b/src/Application/Orders/OrderMapper.cs
@@ -6,7 +6,7 @@ public static class OrderMapper
         Id: order.Id,
         Reference: order.Reference,
         Total: order.Total,
-        CustomerName: order.Customer.FirstName + " " + order.Customer.LastName,
+        CustomerFullName: order.Customer.FirstName + " " + order.Customer.LastName,
         Status: order.Status);
 }
diff --git a/src/Infrastructure/Migrations/Scripts/20261103_rename_customer_name.sql b/src/Infrastructure/Migrations/Scripts/20261103_rename_customer_name.sql
new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/Infrastructure/Migrations/Scripts/20261103_rename_customer_name.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- src/Infrastructure/Migrations/Scripts/20261103_rename_customer_name.sql
+EXEC sp_rename 'Orders.CustomerName', 'CustomerFullName', 'COLUMN';

         var dto = OrderMapper.ToDto(order);
 
         Assert.Equal("Ada Lovelace", dto.CustomerFullName);

 }
